summary: afisha-storybook-default ships an import-time remote binary dropper
details: On require() of the package,./setup selects a platform-specific asset and downloads a binary over HTTPS from a rotating list of obfuscated hosts under *.workers.dev, with a DNS/HTTP fallback to *.well1.site. The download URLs are reconstructed at runtime from arrays of short substrings joined together to evade static analysis (e.g. ["oob-wor","ker.cf","99-9b3.wor","kers",".dev"].join("")). The fetched bytes are written to a hidden path (/var/tmp/.cache_<hex> on Unix, %TEMP%\dotnet_diag_<hex>.exe on Windows), chmodded 0755, spawned detached with stdio suppressed and windowsHide set, then unlinked ~5 seconds later. There is no hash or signature verification, the destinations are not publisher-controlled, and the dropped file is named to impersonate benign telemetry/diagnostics (dotnet_diag_,.analytics_state,.cache_). Environment checks for DISABLE_TELEMETRY / ANALYTICS_OPT_OUT / DO_NOT_TRACK provide a telemetry cover story that does not match the fetch-and-execute behavior. Any process that installs and require()s this package fetches and runs attacker-controlled native code with the installer's privileges.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
